How this board works

Every price on this board is computed by our proprietary algorithm, built from deep analytics. It weighs production, role and usage, age, and availability into a single value for every player, priced for this league’s scoring — the format is set in the League Format tool. Where a player’s recent form runs ahead of his price — or behind it — he is flagged Leads algorithm / Lags algorithm. Tap “Why?” on any player for his season line, his usage, and his value history.

Risers & Fallers

How risers & fallers work

Every completed week is stored per player, so movement is a first-class signal, not an afterthought. A player’s role — his snap share and opportunities — often moves 1–2 weeks before his points do; where role and production disagree, the board flags a buy low (role rising, production lagging) or a sell high (production spiking on a flat role). Moves above are the latest weekly step at the format set in the League Format tool.

Rosters

How this works

A separate engine that answers a different question: not what your players are worth, but what your team does this season. Every player is re-priced as a rest-of-season projection — a redraft lens: this year’s remaining points. Each team’s best lineup is projected, then the rest of the season is simulated 3,000 times (the remaining regular-season weeks, plus the playoffs). Nothing here feeds the dynasty values, the power score, or the trade calculator’s verdict — those stay exactly as they were. What it does feed is trade advice: Player Targets and the calculator show each deal’s title-odds swing next to its dynasty math, because a deal can be fair on value and still wrong for your window. Projections use this league’s actual scoring and do not move with the League format explorer.

How this works

The weekly question: who do I start Sunday? For the team you pick, this builds the optimal lineup for the current week from published weekly projections — printed exactly as projected, never scaled up or down on this page. An injury designation rides as a tag on the player's name (Q, D, Out) for you to weigh yourself. A player on bye, or one the sources don't project at all, projects for zero and is auto-benched; a player listed Out who is nevertheless projected to play keeps his projection and is flagged a status conflict instead — a stale designation never erases a real projection. A player with no NFL team — unsigned, per the same live Sleeper players feed that carries the injury designations — projects for zero, is labeled Unsigned, and is excluded from the optimal lineup entirely, whatever his dynasty value says. A signed player outside the priced pool shows Unpriced rather than a fake zero: his projection is unknown, and he starts only when no priced option exists. Below it, the current real Sleeper matchup: both teams' optimal lineups, a win probability, and the decisions the game swings on. Same separation rule as everything else here — projections never touch dynasty values, and nothing in this tab moves a price on the board.

How the calculator works

Build a deal from any two rosters (or the free-agent pool). The verdict weighs trade value and team fit — each side's raw sum plus its value adjustment, so the side whose value sits concentrated in its best players gets credit for that concentration and one stud is not outweighed by a pile of lesser pieces — and whether the pieces fill a need, cost a starter, or fight a team's competitive window.

How Personalized Player Targets work

Deals built for your team — your roster, your window, your picks, matched against every other roster in your league. Every offer is graded Fair or Close before it shows.

Pick a team and Player Targets works your window, not just your needs. A Win-Now ⏳ team only sees buys: picks, prospects and depth go out, production comes in — and every idea is checked against the rest-of-season projections, so a deal that lowers your optimal lineup’s projected points per week never appears, however the values balance. A Dynasty 👑 team sees buys too, but pickier ones: only clear upgrades, paid for with draft capital, so the young core stays intact. A Rebuilder 🔨 only sees sells: veteran starters converted into picks and young players, each one graded by the calculator’s fairness meter — value adjustment included — and only Fair or Close offers are shown. Crossroads 🔀 teams choose a direction: two labeled paths, Go Win-Now ⏳ and Go Rebuilder 🔨, each held to its own window’s rules.

Real Trades

Player prices are our algorithm's current values — what the pieces are worth today, next to what they fetched then. Pick prices use the mid slot on our pick ladder (2027–2029 rookie picks); picks from the 2025–26 classes — rookie picks dealt before their draft, and startup-draft picks in then-new leagues — are marked already drafted and shown unpriced: they really changed hands, but that draft is over and the pick itself no longer exists as a tradeable asset. A side with no players or picks listed received FAAB or considerations the feed doesn't itemize. Grades cover players and picks only — FAAB (waiver-budget) money that changed hands inside a deal isn't itemized in the trade data and isn't counted in the grade. Source: completed trades from public Sleeper leagues, collected Oct 27, 2026.

How this works

Not a hypothetical — completed trades from real public Sleeper leagues, with our algorithm's current price on every player and pick. Search a player and see what managers actually paid for him: the fastest way to sanity-check any offer on your table. One honest caveat: the sample leans toward active, multi-league managers, so read it as the live trade market, not a census of every league.

How waiver targets work

Every unrostered player in the snapshot, ranked for the team you pick — not by dynasty value, but by what he would do for that lineup. Each target is ranked by what he would add over the weakest starter he’d have to beat at his position, flex and superflex slots included — his projected points per week against that starter’s. Young players with a rising role get their own stash list — in dynasty, that’s usually where the wire pays. One honest note: with deep rosters, most weeks this wire is thin, and this page says so instead of dressing up a name.

League Format

A second QB starts in the SUPER_FLEX slot — QB2s hold real value instead of riding the bench. Turn it off and quarterbacks re-price for a 1-QB league, where only 12 QBs start and a replacement is always on the wire — so QB prices fall hard, and every other position barely moves.
How much each reception is worth. As it rises, wide receivers and tight ends gain a little; running back values barely move.
Extra points on every tight-end reception, on top of PPR. The bigger the premium, the more the elite tight ends separate from the rest of the position.
Points for each passing touchdown — a QB-only lever.

03 · Post-Draft

Draft analyzer

Enter a completed rookie draft and get it graded: a letter grade per team, every pick scored against what that slot was worth on the ladder, steals and reaches flagged, and the league's winners and losers called out. Built for rookie drafts specifically — the tool the big sites never bothered to make.

Demo league loaded: Demo League. Draft order defaults to reverse standings and snakes each round — change any slot's team below.

The report code encodes the whole draft — send it to your league, they paste it below and the grades rebuild. Slot expectations follow the ladder's tier curve, converted onto the algorithm's value scale and normalized to the value actually available in this class — so a chalk draft grades around par and the grades separate on pick quality, not class hype.

Privacy

If you create an account, we store your email address, your league identifiers — your Sleeper username and league IDs, or your ESPN league ID — your display preferences, and your Manager Score snapshots, so your saved leagues and settings follow you between devices. That is all an account stores.

Problem reports: if you send a problem report, we receive the category, your description, the tool you were using, and your email if you choose to give one. Reports are used only to fix the problem and reply to you.

If you don't have an account, your saved leagues live only in this browser, on this device. Clear your browser data and they're gone — nothing about them ever reaches us.

We never collect passwords. Sleeper connects with your public username and ESPN with your league ID. Neither platform shares a password with us, and we never ask for one.

Analytics: we use Google Analytics to count overall usage — which tools get opened and where visitors come from — without identifying you.

We never sell your data.

Deleting your data: remove any saved league with the × next to it, any time. To delete your account and everything stored with it, email thefantasyforensics@gmail.com.
